title: Credit Risk Scoring & Loan Underwriting ML System
problem: Traditional financial underwriting relies heavily on static credit bureau scores that systematically exclude populations lacking extensive formal credit histories. Machine learning credit risk models overcome this barrier by synthesizing transactional banking patterns, behavioral repayment indicators, and alternative cashflow features. Deploying machine learning in credit risk requires rigorous probability calibration, feature monotonicity enforcement to satisfy regulatory fair-lending requirements, automated adverse action factor attribution using SHAP values, and real-time inference latency guarantees.
use_cases: Automated loan default risk assessment for digital consumer lending platforms
Instant credit line underwriting for point-of-sale buy-now-pay-later checkouts
Regulatory adverse action notice generation explaining top negative scoring factors
hard_parts: Handling severe class imbalance (typically < 3% default rates) without inflating false positive rejections
Enforcing monotonic feature constraints in gradient boosting models to satisfy fair lending and financial audit rules
Calibrating raw model logits into empirical probabilities of default using isotonic regression or Platt scaling
Extracting real-time SHAP tree values for adverse action explanation within sub-30ms API response windows
screener_signals: Reproducible ML training pipeline with monotonic feature transformations and cross-validation reports
Calibrated default probability curve verified via Brier score and reliability calibration plots
FastAPI serving endpoint returning default probability and top-3 negative contributing SHAP factors

gradient boosted decision tree framework with monotonic constraint support

components.name: Feature Engineering Pipeline
components.purpose: Computes debt-to-income, cashflow volatility, and Weight of Evidence (WoE) monotonic binnings

components.name: Monotonic XGBoost Model
components.purpose: Trains gradient boosted trees enforcing positive and negative monotonic risk constraints

components.name: Probability Calibration Layer
components.purpose: Transforms raw model margins into well-calibrated default probabilities using Platt scaling

components.name: Adverse Action SHAP Explainer
components.purpose: Extracts top-3 features increasing applicant default probability for regulatory disclosure notices

components.name: Real-Time Underwriting Gateway
components.purpose: Exposes HTTP scoring route returning credit decisions, default probabilities, and reason codes

architecture.data_flow: Applicant financial attributes enter via HTTP POST to FastAPI; Feature Pipeline calculates WoE transformed vectors; XGBoost scores risk margins with monotonic constraints; Probability Calibration Layer maps margin to default probability; SHAP Explainer extracts top adverse contributing features; Gateway returns decision (APPROVE, REVIEW, DECLINE) with calibrated probability and top-3 reason codes.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Monotonic constraints enforced during tree building preventing higher income from increasing default probability; automated decision cutoffs routing high-risk applications to manual review.

targets.method: 5-fold stratified cross-validation evaluated on held-out test split with zero feature leakage
targets.input: Labelled synthetic dataset of 10,000 credit applicant profiles with 2.8% historical default rate
targets.report: Scikit-learn classification report and ROC curve plot export

targets.method: Brier score calculation comparing calibrated predicted default probabilities against true outcomes
targets.input: Held-out test split of 2,000 credit applications across all score deciles
targets.report: Reliability calibration curve plot and decile calibration table

targets.method: Autocannon benchmark measuring duration of feature preprocessing, model scoring, and SHAP extraction
targets.input: 1,000 synthetic applicant requests sent across 10 concurrent HTTP clients
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local loopback network
targets.minimum_pass: p95 decision latency < 45ms per applicant request
targets.target: p95 decision latency < 22ms per applicant request
targets.report: Benchmark latency distribution log and Locust percentile export

starter_input.spec: Tabular credit application dataset with financial attributes (income, debt-to-income, delinquencies, utilization) and default label.
starter_input.size: 10,000 synthetic applicant rows with 18 financial feature columns and binary default flag
starter_input.seeded_cases: Extreme low debt applicants with delinquencies, zero-income outliers, missing credit utilization entries, and high-income applicants

starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly synthetic financial attributes; zero real personal identifiable information, bank accounts, or SSNs used

worksheet.q2: Core path: WoE feature engineering, monotonic XGBoost model, probability calibration, SHAP adverse factors, and FastAPI underwriting endpoint (29h). Extended path: population stability index (PSI) and cashflow time-series models (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Feature Pipeline (5h), XGBoost Training (5h), SHAP Explainability (4h), FastAPI API (4h), Fairness Audit (3h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: ML training, Data analysis/BI. Metrics: ROC-AUC, Brier Score, Underwriting Decision Latency. Rejected: search recall at k (not a recommendation system).

worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: Logistic Regression with statsmodels.
